title: Mount Nemrut near Lake Van erupted at end of Pleistocene
place_text: Mount Nemrut, southwest of Lake Van, Turkey

tellings.quote: exploded and you learn that that mountain last exploded at during the end of the pine during the younger and older dras

plain: Mount Nemrut, a volcano southwest of Lake Van in Turkey, last exploded at the end of the last ice age, during the Younger and Older Dryas, two sudden cold spells of that time. The researcher Matt LaCroix says this without naming a source, in a talk about something big happening around 12,000 BC. He tells it as part of the case that the end of the ice age was a time of violent upheaval.
